header.name: Ecology, Evolution, and Environment
header.description: The goal of this course is to familiarize the students with basic concepts in Ecology, Evolution, and Environmental Science, develop in them an understanding of the current environmental issues and the need for biodiversity conservation.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Describe human induced factors that are responsible for environmental degradation and loss of biodiversity

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Generate hypotheses about how different ecosystem services may be impacted due to climate change

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: A course project will be assigned. Groups of 4-6 studensts will work together on the project.

resources.title: From Individuals to Ecosystems, Michael Begon, Colin R. Townsend and John L. Harper, 2006, Blackwell Publishing, 4th edition.
The Economy of Nature, R.E. Ricklefs, 2008, WH Freeman and Co. 6th edition. (ISBN 9780716738831)
Evolution, D.J. Futuyama, 2009, Sunderland, MA: Sinauer Associates, 2nd edition (ISBN-13: 978-0878932238)
The Ecology of the Changing Planet, Mark B. Bush, 2003, Prentice Hall, 2nd edition (ISBN 0130662577, 9780130662576)
